Criteria (gates): Endpoint count validated and dated; every distribution point in the inventory and the system component inventory; circuit cost and renewal date recorded per office; packaging inventory complete; the ask stated as acquisition or five-year cost with scope itemized; a dated target DP count; the worksheet reviewed and stored inside the boundary

Phase: Phase 1 — Decision on the funding ask, and Stage 1 in a test hierarchy
Name: Decision on the funding ask
Options (decisions): Refresh in place; consolidate to a hub tier (the guide's recommendation where the circuits allow); cloud-first with Connected Cache, keeping a hub tier only until the five gates close
If late (decisions): Refresh money is committed by default, or the hub build can't start

Phase: Phase 1 — Decision on the funding ask, and Stage 1 in a test hierarchy
Name: Budget submission revised to the chosen option, the worked case's planning assumptions replaced by Phase 0 data, and its consistency with Intune-first stated

Phase: Phase 1 — Decision on the funding ask, and Stage 1 in a test hierarchy
Name: Gate 1 — Funding decision recorded
Criteria (gates): Option chosen with the decision table and worksheet as its evidence; budget submission revised; target DP count and fiscal year recorded; the decision filed in the program's decision register

Phase: Phase 1 — Decision on the funding ask, and Stage 1 in a test hierarchy
Name: Stage 1: Lab 2 run end to end in a test hierarchy, every change applied and then backed out from its plan.csv

Phase: Phase 1 — Decision on the funding ask, and Stage 1 in a test hierarchy
Name: Stage 1 to Stage 2: go/no-go for production
Owner or approver: Content delivery project lead and ISSO
Options (decisions): Go when Lab 2 ran end to end with its back-out, every cmdlet ran on the agency's Configuration Manager version, the inventory matched the console and the change board approved the production plan; no-go repeats Stage 1
If late (decisions): No production change can start, and the hub build waits

Name: Hub sites and distribution points per hub
Owner or approver: Endpoint lead and network engineering lead
Options (decisions): Existing regional facilities inside the current boundary, two pull DPs each, with source DPs at the two data centers (the worked case: 12 sites, 24 DPs); more hubs where latency or headcount needs them
If late (decisions): Hub servers can't be ordered or built

Name: Hub DP servers built on Windows Server 2019 or later: IIS, BITS and Remote Differential Compression; CM-6 baseline applied and scanned; HTTPS with a PKI certificate; added to the inventory and the SSP
Pull DPs added at each hub, sourcing from the data center DPs; one distribution point group per hub (New-DpcHubTier.ps1 -Apply)
Content distributed to each hub group; distribution status clean; content validation run; inventory rerun
Gate 2 — Hub tier serving content
Criteria (gates): Every hub DP in production, baselined, scanned and in the SSP; every package distributed to its region's group with no failures; load per DP under 3,200 clients (80% of the published 4,000); change records for every server

Phase: Phase 3 — Peer caching and boundary groups
Name: Boundary groups for the pilot wave: hub DPs added, peer options set, the other hubs as timed fallback, never to the default site group (Set-DpcBoundaryGroups.ps1 -Apply)

Phase: Phase 3 — Peer caching and boundary groups
Name: Client-to-client traffic on branch segments: TCP 8003, UDP 8004 and TCP 7680
Options (decisions): Allow within each office's subnet only; allow for named peer cache sources only; block, and size circuits for hub pulls
If late (decisions): Peer cache and Delivery Optimization peering can't be configured, and the pilot measures nothing

Phase: Phase 3 — Peer caching and boundary groups
Name: Co-management on for the pilot collection (Endpoint plan E1.4)
If late (decisions): Pilot devices have no Intune channel for Delivery Optimization policy

Phase: Phase 3 — Peer caching and boundary groups
Name: Peer cache sources chosen per pilot office (desktop chassis, disk, always on); client settings deployed; partial download on; BranchCache enabled

Phase: Phase 3 — Peer caching and boundary groups
Name: Delivery Optimization through Intune: Group download mode with a group ID per office, or subnet restriction, for the pilot devices

Phase: Phase 3 — Peer caching and boundary groups
Name: Pilot measurement at the pilot offices: bytes from peers, from the hub and from the office DP, for a month of deployments

Phase: Phase 3 — Peer caching and boundary groups
Name: Gate 3 — Pilot offices served from hubs and peers
Criteria (gates): Pilot offices' content served by the hub and peers, with the office DP in read-only fallback and serving under a threshold the endpoint lead sets; no deployment failure traced to content location; measurement report filed

Name: Pilot sites governed and evidenced on new transport (Network plan Gate 3)
If late (decisions): The pilot offices are still on their old circuits, and the first wave of DP retirements waits

Name: Pilot wave: each office DP checked, drained, watched 30 days, removed with its site system; disks sanitized; inventory and SSP updated
Wave plan: offices ordered by circuit readiness and renewal date
Options (decisions): By circuit readiness and renewal (the guide's order); by region (simpler, but waits on the slowest circuit in each)
If late (decisions): Wave 2 can't be scheduled, and offices keep DPs they no longer need

Name: Wave 2, about 25% of offices: boundary groups moved, peers enabled, office DPs read-only, then retired after 30 clean days
Wave 3, about 60% of offices cumulative
Wave 4, every remaining office, or a dated exception with its reason
Gate 4 — No branch distribution point left
Criteria (gates): Every office DP retired or in the exception register with a date and reason; every retired server's media sanitized and its inventory and SSP entries closed; hub load per DP still under 80% of the published limit

Name: Packaging standard
Options (decisions): PSAppDeployToolkit as the standard wrapper, version pinned, for every app that isn't a clean MSI; vendor installers with Intune's PowerShell script installer only; a mix by app class
If late (decisions): Repackaging can't start, and the client apps workload waits

Name: Standard template: pinned toolkit version, signed scripts, one log path, exit codes mapped, detection rule pattern; held under change control
Catalog rationalized: apps nobody installs retired, duplicate versions removed, an owner for every app kept
Most-installed apps repackaged on the template; each tested from Configuration Manager and as an .intunewin from Intune
Rest of the catalog repackaged or retired
Gate 5 — Catalog on the standard wrapper
Criteria (gates): Every kept app has an owner, a package on the template, a tested detection rule and a change record; the same package installs from either tool; retired apps removed from both

Name: Client apps and Office Click-to-Run apps workloads: Pilot Intune, then Intune; apps published as Win32 apps from the standard packages
Configuration Manager required and available deployments withdrawn as each app moves; the count reported weekly
Workloads cut over, including Windows Update policies and device configuration (Endpoint plan Gate 3)
If late (decisions): Update content still comes from Configuration Manager, and retirement gate 2 can't close

Name: Configuration Manager software-update client setting turned off for every device on the Windows Update workload
Intune-first intake with Autopilot registration (Endpoint plan E1.5)
If late (decisions): There's no Autopilot path to move bare-metal provisioning onto

Name: OS provisioning for existing devices
Options (decisions): Windows Autopilot for every rebuild, with reset where it applies; keep task sequences for a named exception class on a hub DP until it can move
If late (decisions): Imaging keeps a PXE distribution point alive, and retirement gate 3 stays open

Name: Bare-metal provisioning moved from task sequences to Autopilot; PXE turned off on every DP
Compliance and Endpoint Protection evidence sourced from Intune and Defender, not the Configuration Manager site database; ISSO confirms

Phase: Phase 7 — Connected Cache at the hubs
Name: Connected Cache form and placement
Options (decisions): Connected Cache for Enterprise and Education on its own host at each hub, its Azure resource placed in the boundary analysis; the Configuration Manager-integrated cache on a hub DP with no other roles (then retirement gate 4 binds it); none, where measured circuits carry cloud content
If late (decisions): Cloud content keeps crossing every hub circuit, and gate 4 has no plan

Phase: Phase 7 — Connected Cache at the hubs
Name: Cache hosts built at the hubs on a supported OS, nothing else on port 80; Delivery Optimization pointed at each office's hub cache

Phase: Phase 7 — Connected Cache at the hubs
Name: Cache hit rate measured; Win32 app, update and Microsoft 365 Apps content confirmed served from the hubs

Phase: Phase 7 — Connected Cache at the hubs
Name: Connected Cache turned off on any DP hardware once the hub cache serves that office
Retirement gate 1 — App content
Criteria (gates): Client apps and Office Click-to-Run workloads on Intune for the whole validated population, and no required or available deployment still published from Configuration Manager

Name: Retirement gate 2 — Update content
Criteria (gates): Windows Update policies and device configuration workloads on Intune, and Configuration Manager's software-update client setting off for those devices

Name: Retirement gate 3 — OS provisioning
Criteria (gates): Bare-metal provisioning on Autopilot; no task sequence or PXE service still in use

Name: Retirement gate 4 — Caching role
Criteria (gates): No Connected Cache instance runs on distribution-point hardware, or none is needed on the measured circuits

Name: Retirement gate 5 — Compliance evidence
Criteria (gates): Compliance and Endpoint Protection reporting no longer cite the Configuration Manager site database as their evidence source

Name: Retire the hub distribution point tier
Predecessors: RG1, RG2, RG3, RG4, RG5, CG4, CG5
Options (decisions): Retire it in the week the last gate closes; keep it while any gate is open. Never on a date alone
If late (decisions): Twenty-odd servers stay in the boundary to be patched, scanned and accredited for no workload

Name: Hub and source DPs drained and removed with their site systems (Invoke-DpcOfficeRetirement.ps1 -GatesPath); media sanitized; inventory and SSP entries closed
Cleanup: distribution point groups removed, boundary group site-system references cleared, peer cache client settings and deployments retired; no DP role left in the hierarchy
Gate 8 — Last distribution point retired, site roles cleaned up, evidence complete
Criteria (gates): All five retirement gates closed in a gates run; no distribution point role left in Get-CMSiteRole; every DP's decommission record, sanitization record and SSP change filed; the content delivery evidence set in the guide's requirements table complete

Name: Program G3 — Rollout Complete
